rationale: bugs_open/248 (slug cta_recompute_clobbers_authored_contact_links). One set, areasExcludedFromCTA={about,contact,privacy,terms,legal}, makes three different decisions and only the first is a claim it can support: (1) chooseCTATargets' rank() uses it to stop a FRESHLY PICKED CTA landing on a utility page - sound; (2) applyCTARecompute's keep-branch uses it to judge an ALREADY-STORED url as untrustworthy - this is the bug; (3) check_misdirected_cta uses it to call a deployed utility href an 'unknown destination' and file it for a human - 103 items filed, 103 still open, and an independent 2026-08-07 audit found 18 of 18 sampled were CORRECT contact buttons. Decisions (2) and (3) treat 'the platform should not GENERATE this' as evidence of 'a human did not MEAN this', which it never was. Consequence: a CTA reading 'Get in touch' -> /contact.html is replaced by an unrelated tool page on the next cta_links_stale rerender, because generic contact copy names no page (get/in are stopwords) so the label-match branch declines, the keep-branch refuses it for its area, and the positional pick takes it. This is not theoretical and is no longer dormant: the bug file's containment argument (schedulers disabled) expired when site-discovery-rotation-completeness was re-enabled on 2026-08-16 and detected-item-promoter began promoting detected->triaged every 900s. On 2026-08-17 19:11:24Z a misdirected_cta item carrying reason=cta_links_stale completed on finetuning.uk/services and, in the same second, rewrote primary_cta_url from /contact.html to /tools/password-entropy.html while leaving the label 'Start a Conversation' untouched - one instance of the mechanism confirmed in production, with the copy still standing on the live page as evidence of intent. 18 components fleet-wide remain in the at-risk state; 13 are hero/call-to-action, the only functions either writer can reach, and 8 of those are webdesign.uk including its homepage hero. A FOURTH consumer had the same defect and nobody had filed it: setCTAField, the build/regeneration writer, has no keep-branch at all, so fixing only the repair path leaves every authored contact link dying on the next full regeneration. The fix the bug file wanted (candidate 1) was a provenance field on content_data, costed there as the largest change and needing a backfill. It is unnecessary: the code already constrains itself enough to DERIVE provenance. The positional pick cannot choose a utility page (rank() drops those candidates by URL shape) and the label match cannot return one once candidatesFromHubs applies the same filter - so a stored url that is BOTH a valid page AND in a utility area was not written by either writer. Validity is load-bearing: an INVALID /contact.html is bugs_open/203's phantom and must stay recomputable.

plan.summary: Split one set's three jobs. rank() keeps its job unchanged (a fresh pick still never lands on a utility page). A new shared predicate storedCTADestinationIsAuthored expresses the DIFFERENT question 'could the resolver have produced this stored url?', and both writers consult it: applyCTARecompute stops refusing utility-area destinations, and setCTAField gains the keep-branch it never had. candidatesFromHubs gains the filter its own doc comment already falsely claimed, which is what makes the predicate's invariant exact rather than approximate. The detector's excluded-area arm is DEMOTED - it still emits its finding, it no longer files a work item. Register entry LNK-033 ships in the same commit per the ordering exemption's condition (2).

edits.rationale: The named seam. Provenance derived from the resolver's own constraints instead of recorded in a field. Its doc comment states the invariant, both consumers, and - the part that matters for review - exactly what breaks it at a distance: widening the hub/interactive loaders, removing candidatesFromHubs' filter, removing rank()'s test, or a utility-area schema fallback on any ctaFieldNames component. Any of those lets the resolver mint the urls the predicate calls authored, and both keep branches would then freeze the resolver's own output.

The reported defect. The single keep-branch becomes two explicit ones. The AUTHORED branch writes the value rather than returning bare, so the keep cannot be beaten by anything else that populated ResolvedData (which merges last); the ORDINARY branch is byte-identical to today, including its bare return, so the existing 'leaves fields untouched' contract test passes unchanged. The label-match branch above both is untouched and still wins - 248's own verification bar #2.

The unfiled half: this writer had no keep-branch of any kind, so an authored contact link died on the next full regeneration regardless of the repair path. Takes the slot's stored content_data, already in hand at the call site as `existing` - no new loader, no extra query. WRITES rather than skipping: a regeneration replaces the row, plan_sections' carry misses on non-deployed rows, conflicted duplicate slots and mismatched slot names, and a gated template renders no button for an absent url - so a branch added to KEEP a link must not be able to delete it. Positioned after the label match and before the positional pick, so a fabricated contact url whose label names a real page is still repaired.

Its doc comment claimed 'both lists are already filtered (excluded areas, the page's own URL) by chooseCTATargets' own rank()'. That was never true - rank() builds a filtered LOCAL slice and never mutates its inputs, and both call sites pass the raw loader output. 4 live section-index pages sit at utility URLs, so the label branch could mint one, which would falsify the predicate above. Applying the filter here makes the claim true and the invariant exact. URL-shape test rather than page_type, because a section-index hub can legitimately live at /contact/index.html.

DEMOTED, not deleted: the finding is still emitted, the cta_names_unknown_destination work item is not. Its premise - a utility page is never a legitimate CTA target - is exactly what this change overturns for stored links, and its measured precision is ~0 (103 filed, 103 open, 18/18 sampled correct). Deletion was considered and rejected because it is the only arm that can see a fabricated-but-VALID contact link: the phantom arm goes blind once the contact page exists and the misdirect arm goes blind when the copy names no page. Demoting keeps that signal in discovery output while ending a queue nobody can drain.

edits.rationale: Flagged separately because it is the one edit not strictly about the exclusion split. This read is keyed by slot_name and last-row-wins, and it NOW decides whether an authored destination is kept - so on the 11 pages fleet-wide that legitimately carry a duplicate slot_name the decision was nondeterministic, and an unfiltered read let a section someone had REMOVED drive it. Adds build_status IS DISTINCT FROM 'removed' (not !=, because the column is nullable and != would silently drop every NULL-status row) and ORDER BY position, matching the fix already made in rerender_page_sections' loadStoredSections.

edits.rationale: Seven tests. The bug file's A/B repro as the CORRECT assertion with its control in the same function; the predicate's own unit test including the arm that keeps 203 repairable (invalid /contact.html -> false); ordering pins on BOTH writers; a NEGATIVE CONTROL proving an ordinary stored destination is still re-derived (without it, a fix that froze every CTA would pass everything else here); and the ASYMMETRY PIN, which asserts in one function that a fresh pick still refuses a utility page, that the candidate set refuses one, and that a stored one is kept - so re-merging the two uses goes red rather than making 13 live contact buttons go quiet. All three edits were mutation-checked against a clean HEAD tree: reverting each one turns the matching test red.

Condition (2) of the ordering exemption: a shared seam with two writers and a detector is registered in the SAME commit that ships it, with its landmine and open question written down rather than left to become folklore. Index row added in the same commit.
edits.sketch: Append a new register entry LNK-033 to link-management.md and its row to 000_concept_index.md, recording: the predicate and its two consumers; the invariant (no resolver path can emit a utility-area url, positional via rank(), label-match via candidatesFromHubs' new filter); the asymmetry (fresh pick refuses, stored link kept) and the test that pins it; the LANDMINE that the invariant is breakable at a distance by widening the hub loaders, dropping either filter, or adding a utility-area schema fallback to a ctaFieldNames component; and the known residual that a single incidental shared token still beats an authored contact link.

grounded_in: bugs_open/248: 'So a CTA already pointing into any excluded area can never take the keep branch. It then needs the label-match branch above it to save it - and genuine contact copy is exactly the copy that matches nothing.'

bugs_closed/023:405-410: 'That exclusion is sensible as a default for a generated CTA and wrong as an absolute - it needs an authored-intent escape hatch.' (Identified the right fix in 2026-07-19 and closed without building it.)

016b debugging guide, s9: 'A guard phrased as a whitelist of sensible destinations is doing two jobs, and they have opposite risk profiles... When one set serves both a generative and a validating decision, splitting it is usually the cheap fix.'

The 2026-07-14 design note that created the conflation - PLAN_from_ultraplan_vonc_internal_links_fixes.md:79-80: 'Exception rule - do not clobber authored links... Keep it if it resolves to a real page AND is not an excluded destination... Reuse it in chooseCTATargets' area filter too so the two agree.' The rule's own title states the intent this fix restores.

plan.risks: A machine-written but VALID utility url would now be frozen rather than churned. Bounded and measured rather than argued: every remaining at-risk row postdates 2026-07-14, when migration 091 removed the unconditional pages.contact writer, so no pre-migration residue remains in the at-risk set. The worst case is a WORKING link to the contact page (validPages membership is part of the predicate), against a destroyed authored link as the harm prevented. The label-match branch still wins on a single incidental shared token ('Talk to us about pricing' -> a Pricing page), so this does not close every case. Forced by verification bar #2; recorded as a residual in the bug file and the register entry rather than papered over. Demoting the detector arm removes 103 review items. Nothing consumes that item type - revalidate_review_queue deliberately registers no revalidator for it, test-pinned - and the other four arms still file, so the type and its tests survive. The invariant is breakable at a distance by code that never mentions the predicate. That is why it is a register entry with a landmine and an asymmetry test, not just a function. NOT in this change, deliberately: widening the candidate set so copy naming contact can RESOLVE to contact (bugs_closed/023's forward direction). 149 detector findings suggest a utility page the repairer cannot produce and so re-detect for ever, but closing that ADDS a capability with a measured false-match risk ('about' is deliberately not a stopword per the 2026-08-08 calibration) and would falsify this predicate's invariant unless real provenance lands first. Filed separately; the owner-commissioned cta_target_content_pass lane already holds the adjacent question.
